pr_title: Do not retry client requests when failing with ContentTooLargeException
pr_body:
The default configuration of the Low Level Rest Client is to buffer the response body up to 100 MB. If that threshold is exceeded, a `ContentTooLargeException` is thrown in the lower layers of LLRC.

When such an exception occurs, LLRC will retry the request, which has some bad side effects:
- for idempotent requests like a regular search, there's no point in retrying since the response will always be too large.
- for scroll searches, retrying will move to the next scroll slice. With a cluster big enough or a number of scroll slices small enough, retrying may reach the last scroll slice, which is usually be smaller and may fit into the buffer limit. From an application perspective, the request will have succeeded with the last slice as result, despite having effectively skipped a large amount of results.

This PR fixes that, by ensuring that no retry happens if a request fails with a `ContentTooLargeException`.

Fixes #86041.

I added the `v6.8.24` label to backport to 6.8 as this was found by a customer still using 6.8 and even if there's no additional 6.8 release, they may want to use a snapshot version with the fix.

issue_context.title: Low level rest client retrying scrolls, skipping pages
issue_context.body:
### Elasticsearch Version

Doesn't matter

### Installed Plugins

_No response_

### Java Version

all

### OS Version

doesn't matter

### Problem Description

When you send a `scroll` request to the low level rest client it uses it's standard retry mechanism which catches all errors and just retries against another ES instance. The trouble with that is that you *can't* retry a scroll - it generally consumes state on the server and moves to the next page.

### Steps to Reproduce

Scroll with low level rest client.

### Logs (if relevant)

_No response_
comments:
Ideas for remediation:
1. Document that you should turn off retry for scroll. Document how to do it.
2. Detect scroll and automatically disable retry.
3. Never retry a `ContentTooLargeException`

This could also be a problem with reindex. I'm not sure. It uses the low level REST client directly.

Certainly the high level rest client shouldn't retry scrolls.

We discussed this in the distributed team. If clients can come up with a generic solution to this (i.e., not retry scroll requests), reindex should be solved by that too. In case we need to change how reindex instantiates the rest-client, we are more than happy to do so. But we would be looking towards input from the clients team first on the path to solving this for the low-level client in general.

I looked at the issue. It was found in version 6 and still exists in 7 and 8.

> Document that you should turn off retry for scroll. Document how to do it.
  Detect scroll and automatically disable retry.
  Never retry a `ContentTooLargeException`

The reliable way to address this is to not retry on `ContentTooLargeException`. This exception is thrown client-side when the ES server has sent a response that is too large (100 MB by default).

Disabling retries alltogether for scroll will also miss some errors were retrying would be ok, such as when the client wasn't able to send the request. Retries should however not happen once the request has been sent: if there's e.g. a connection loss, a read timeout or even a 5xx response. In those cases we don't know if ES has received and (even partially) processed the request and modified its internal state.

Now this not only applies to scroll, but also to any non idempotent request sent to Elasticsearch. Unfortunately it's hard to determine idempotency by looking at the HTTP request without deeper knowledge of API specifics: for example the `/search/_scroll` endpoint accepts the `GET` method that we could assume to be idempotent but isn't.

I opened PR #87248 to not retry on `ContentTooLargeException`.
